summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs. The policy and behavior persisted through a verified node restart; RHEL release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the missing opsadmin local account.
Installed /etc/cron.allow with exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0600 and the correct SELinux context.
Verified root and opsadmin can install crontabs while nobody is denied.
Safely restarted node1 and verified complete recovery and policy persistence.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: The allowlist contains exactly root and opsadmin. Direct pre- and post-restart tests show both permitted users can install crontabs, while nobody receives an access-denied response. Test crontabs were cleaned up.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel

evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline boot ID 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146, reboot acknowledgment, changed boot ID be078787-13e6-4445-89e4-76a664ac399f, and full post-restart recovery with the system running, crond active/enabled, policy intact, behavioral checks passing, and no test spool files remaining.
